verdict.rationale: The only client-side evidence is in PostHog Desktop, whose docs say coding agents running inside it get "Other MCP servers for services such as issue trackers, design tools, and internal APIs" alongside PostHog's own MCP server. That is a single thin mention, and those agents are third-party (Claude Code, Codex, Pi) hosted in Desktop. Most other MCP evidence covers PostHog serving MCP tools to outside clients, which does not count for this story. Missing for 10: documentation of how to add or configure external MCP servers, evidence that PostHog AI in the web app or Slack can use third-party MCP tools, and any hands-on or independent corroboration.
